title: Every 3D transition is easy and always works: pick one for two touching clips and Photonz makes it happen
goal: None of the 3D transitions (Flip, Cube, Swing, Doorway, Revolve, Push in depth) are usable today. When two clips touch and the person picks a transition, Photonz does whatever it takes to make it happen: it uses spare footage where there is some, holds the edge frames where there is none, and adjusts the clips' positions on the timeline if the transition needs it. It never refuses with a message the person cannot act on. Dragging one clip to overlap the next must also end in a working transition or be impossible, never two clips stacked with no cut.
notes: Reported by the user 2026-10-29 in the intake window, frustrated: 'There's no way I have ever been able to use this transition. I can't see how you can get it to work.' and 'If I have two clips that are butt up against each other, and I have a cube transition, wouldn't it just pause the frame on one? And then pause the frame on the other and rotate the view, and then play the other one when the transition's done? This is so unintuitive.' Code today: a cut's transition is fitted to spare footage either side (ClipCut.fitted) and refused with noSpare when there is none; a clip's right-click aims at BOTH its ends (TransitionTargets.swift transitionTargets(ofClip:)) and a free end refuses every kind but dissolve and dip to black with needsTwoClips; editPoints(onTrack:) counts two clips as meeting only at a gap of exactly 0 ms, so an overlap on one track is no cut at all. The user's first recording (Recording 2026-10-28 at 14.21.13, 9.147 s) was used to its last frame, so Cube had no spare on that side. Premiere does the transition anyway with repeated frames ('Insufficient media. This transition will contain repeated frames'); Final Cut offers to overlap or uses freeze frames. The user was running the timeline-room-history-drop worktree's dev build when this happened.
acceptance: The user's rule, 2026-10-29: two clips that touch plus a 3D transition picked = the transition happens. Photonz adjusts what it must (holds frames, slides or trims the clips, ripples what follows) to make room, as one undoable step, and the canvas shows the result playing. No refusal for lack of spare footage, at any door: right-click on the cut, right-click on either clip, the picker at the cut, the Transitions panel drag, the default transition key, and the agent tool set_transition.

Every 3D kind (Flip, Cube, Swing, Doorway, Revolve, Push in depth) and every other overlap kind (dissolve, push, wipe, blur through) passes the same walk with two DIFFERENT recordings, each used to its last and first frame.

Try path at Next defaults: put two different recordings on one track so they touch, the first used to its very last frame (no spare), right-click the cut or either clip, choose Add Transition then Cube. Cube goes on and plays: the outgoing clip holds its last frame and the incoming clip its first while the cube turns, then the incoming clip plays on. The same for every kind that needs an overlap (dissolve, push, wipe, blur through, flip, swing, doorway, revolve, push in depth).
Where there IS spare footage it is still used as today. Held frames are used only for the part that has none, on each side separately.

Right-click on a CLIP whose one end touches another clip and whose other end touches nothing: the transition goes on the cut, and the notice says nothing failed. Today it reports 'Cube needs a clip on both sides' because the free end refused, which reads as if the whole thing failed. A refused free end is never the headline when the cut took it.

Two clips dragged to overlap on the same track (the user did this on 2026-10-29: 0 to 9.147 s and 8.176 to 18.248 s on V2, which the document reads as having no cut at all): decide and build the Premiere/Final Cut answer. Either a drag on one track can never leave an overlap (it trims or ripples, as Premiere's overwrite does), or the overlap becomes the transition's length. No state where two clips sit on top of each other on one track and the timeline shows no cut.

The agent tool set_transition and the timeline agree on what a cut is. Measured today: read_document listed a cut at 9.147 s while the clips touched; the tool refused only after they overlapped. Add a walk with two DIFFERENT recordings touching (the existing transitions-in-depth-at-a-cut walk uses one sample recording cut in two, which always has spare footage, so it never met this case).

Walks: Cube between two touching recordings with no spare, by right-click on the cut, right-click on each clip and the Transitions panel drag; the overlap case. A filmed reel of the cube turning across the held frames goes in the audit under queue/audits/.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
